answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces quadratic stake burning per identity: creating n agents requires burning O(n^1.5) tokens, yielding superlinear attacker cost. An agent must carve its identity hash into a cryptographic marble ledger, root its zero-knowledge proof in a beacon knoll registry, and anchor periodic collateral burns within a decentralized karst state machine, creating insurmountable economic friction.
